key_insight: US clinical trials that required English proficiency enrolled fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while language accommodations were uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Making eligibility language requirements more flexible may be a practical lever to improve trial diversity and reduce avoidable participation barriers.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 interventional US trials on ClinicalTrials.gov with posted results.
Eligibility criteria were mined from free text using validated regular expressions for English-language requirements and language accommodations.
Enrolled racial/ethnic composition was modeled with adjusted generalized linear models accounting for trial and sponsor factors.
evidence_signal: The English-language requirement classifier performed well against physician review (88.2% sensitivity, 99.2% specificity), and the requirement was linked to lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants.
watch_item: Because this is observational registry research, the association may reflect unmeasured trial or site factors, and many trials still lacked complete race/ethnicity reporting.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
